title: Honda Civic Engines by Year (1973–2026)
description: Every factory engine in the US Honda Civic by year, 1973–2026: the CVCC fours, the D-series, the VTEC engines of the Si and Type R, the hybrids and turbos.
intro: Honda brought the Civic to the US for 1973. Every Civic engine has been a four-cylinder; hybrid ratings are for engine and motor combined. The del Sol, sold as a Civic through 1995, is included.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: First generation
intro: The 1.2 EB and, from 1975, the 1.5 CVCC stratified-charge engine.

generations.name: Third generation
intro: The 1.3 and 1.5 CVCC engines, the CRX HF and the fuel-injected Si.

generations.name: Fourth generation
intro: The 1.5 D15B engines and the 1.6 D16A6 in the Si.

generations.name: Fifth generation
intro: The D15 and D16 engines, the lean-burn VX, and the B16A3 VTEC in the del Sol.

generations.name: Sixth generation
intro: The D16Y engines, the CNG GX and the B16A2 in the 1999–2000 Si.

generations.name: Seventh generation
intro: The 1.7 D17 engines, the K20A3 in the Si hatchback and the first Civic Hybrid.

generations.name: Eighth generation
intro: The 1.8 R18 and the 2.0 K20Z3 in the Si.

generations.name: Ninth generation
intro: The 1.8 R18, the 2.4 K24 in the Si and the 1.5 Hybrid.

generations.name: Tenth generation
intro: The 2.0 K20C2, the 1.5 turbo, and the 2.0 turbo K20C1 in the Type R from 2017.

generations.name: Eleventh generation
intro: The 2.0 and 1.5 turbo, the Si and Type R, and the two-motor hybrid from 2025.

excluded.name: 1.8L / 110 inline-four
excluded.researchNote: Consumer Guide covers the GX from 2008 (retail expansion); Honda 2006 specs and EPA show it from 2006. No engine code stated. Only one independent source located for this year; withhold or re-check.

excluded.name: 1.5L / 91 inline-four turbo
excluded.researchNote: Center-exit exhaust, premium fuel. 2018-2019 rating carried over (no year-specific hp source fetched). KBB 2020 lists the Sport and Sport Touring hatch at 174 hp and the LX hatch with the 2.0 - both contradicted by Honda 2020 and EPA (no 2.0 hatch before 2022); KBB hatch data not used. Only one independent source located for this year; withhold or re-check.

excluded.name: 2.0L / 122 inline-four turbo
excluded.researchNote: Wikipedia (10th gen) gives 315 hp for the 2017-2021 Type R, which is the 2023 FL5 figure; Honda and KBB give 306 (Wikipedia not counted). Only one independent source located for this year; withhold or re-check.

excluded.name: 1.5L / 91 inline-four turbo
excluded.researchNote: Center-exit exhaust, premium fuel. 2018-2019 rating carried over (no year-specific hp source fetched). KBB 2020 lists the Sport and Sport Touring hatch at 174 hp and the LX hatch with the 2.0 - both contradicted by Honda 2020 and EPA (no 2.0 hatch before 2022); KBB hatch data not used. Only one independent source located for this year; withhold or re-check.

excluded.name: 2.0L / 122 inline-four turbo
excluded.researchNote: No Type R for 2022. Wikipedia gives 330 PS (325 hp), a JDM/EU rating; US SAE net is 315 (Wikipedia not counted). Honda also publishes 2024 and 2026 Type R spec sheets. Only one independent source located for this year; withhold or re-check.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
